successors.note: The Aedui were 'not conquered' but kept their laws and title and received Roman citizenship; Pliny lists Augustodunum among the civitates foederatae. The roman-republic dossier takes central Gaul in 58-52 as a gain from 'Gallic tribes'.

capitals.name: Bibracte (Mont Beuvray)
capitals.note: 'Bibracte (on Mont Beuvray, the principal oppidum, abandoned toward the end of the 1st century BC)'; Augustodunum (Autun) was founded at Augustus's order around the end of the 1st century BC. The page does not date Bibracte's primacy; the span is the life (confidence 1).

ledger.note: c. 150 BC: the Aedui, Rome's first inner-Gaulish allies. 'The alliance was concluded around 150-140 BC' (undated) and they were allies 'from the middle of the 2nd century BC'; a foedus aequum, and 'fratres populi Romani' in Tacitus. The page gives no founding of the tribe; 150 is the first date the page offers (page silent).

wars.name: Gallic Wars: Caesar's intervention against Ariovistus (58 BC)
wars.outcome: Caesar intervened 'at the Aedui's request' against the Germani of Ariovistus, allied with the Sequani; Diviciacus guided the legions into Alsace. No Aeduan border moved.
wars.note: The page is silent on the 71-58 dates of Ariovistus's war and on the battle of Magetobriga; Diviciacus's appeal to the Senate against the Sequani, Arverni and Germani failed in 61.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Thin: no infobox, no area; the page is silent on Ariovistus's dates (71-58), Magetobriga, the Boii settled with the Aedui in 58, Litaviccus and Noviodunum. Start 150 and the 100 client tie are confidence 1. The end at 52 matches the Arverni dossier and roman-republic's 52 gain; strictly the Aedui were never conquered, so a gap-filler may prefer a vassal-of-Rome treatment to 27 BC (Alesia page: provinces under Augustus in 27 BC). roman-republic's counterpart 'Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)' omits the Aedui.
